title: Chess, But My Pieces Can Time Travel
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where the player has a one-time power: one piece may travel back in time to any square it occupied within its last three moves, without changing the rest of the position. The jump uses a turn and can capture an enemy piece now standing on that old square. Narrator tours his queen around so that the enemy queen may later step onto one of her past squares, then eventually wins with a ladder mate after a long game.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600).

Once per game, the player may 'time travel' one piece: double-click a piece to see its past squares (the squares it stood on before each of its last up to 3 moves, e.g. a bishop moved once can only return to c1).
The time-travel move replaces the player's normal move for that turn; the rest of the board is unchanged.
If an enemy piece now stands on the target past square, it is captured [inferred from plan 'teleport my queen back and win this queen outright'].
Past squares are per-piece history; once a piece has moved more than 3 times, older squares are no longer available ('I've lost the ability to move to b5').
Presumably cannot leave own king in check [inferred].
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish (ladder mate in the video).
